text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 fired: `catalog-service.model-config` — abnormal model defaults pushed to prod. Incident ID: INC-20260314-0821. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-20260314-0821

pagerduty: Paging: on-call (sam) — please acknowledge 

sam: acked. Taking triage. I'm seeing a spike in generation errors and malformed token outputs from recently promoted catalog revision. Customers report corrupted tokens mid-stream.

sam: quick summary -> traffic to /v1/generate for model `redwood/gpt-3x` started returning tokenization errors ~08:18 UTC. Error rate ~12% across regions, SLO breach risk.

alex: @sam thanks. Any signs it's infra or model config?

sam: logs point to mismatch between model binary revision and tokenizer expectation. The catalog entry for `redwood/gpt-3x:prod` was promoted two hours ago to `rev-20260314-b` but the tokenizer field still references `tokenizer-v1`. The rev requires `tokenizer-v2` (breaking change).

cheng: posting relevant config snippet from catalog (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/gpt-3x",
  "revision": "rev-20260314-b",
  "tokenizer": "tokenizer-v1",
  "defaults": { "max_tokens": 2048 }
}
```

cheng: expected tokenizer should be `tokenizer-v2`. That explains decode failures.

ida: can we hotfix by pinning the catalog to previous stable revision while we assess?

sam: yes. Mitigation plan: 1) Pin `prod` to `rev-20260314-a` (last known good) 2) Add immediate sentinel check in router to reject requests routed to mismatched tokenizer + fallback to stable variant 3) Notify impacted customers/support -> triage & postmortem.

sam: I'm going to pin now. Calling `redwoodctl`

sam: ```bash
# pin prod back to stable
redwoodctl catalog set-default --model redwood/gpt-3x --revision rev-20260314-a --env prod
```

cheng: running the command now in stage/ops account...

cheng: output:
```
Applying default revision... success
Propagating to routing layer... success
Estimated propagation: ~15s
```

sam: routing propagation shows success. Starting canary validation on 5% traffic.

leda: support notified via internal ticket (SUP-783). Customer-facing note drafted, cc: product. No high-paying enterprise customers on the affected route yet, likely majority are dev/prod self-serve.

alex: good. @sam monitor latency/errors for next 30m. If errors drop to baseline, we can close pager and do a rollback PR in the catalog repo to fix tokenizer metadata and add CI check.

sam: monitoring -> errors dropped from 12% to 0.9% after pin. Latency unchanged. Canary looks healthy.

incident-bot: Note added to incident INC-20260314-0821: mitigation (pinned to rev-20260314-a) applied by sam.

ida: next steps for root cause: why was revision promoted without tokenizer bump? Was this automated promotion from CI or manual?

cheng: preliminary: promotion pipeline picks a manifest from s3. It looks like the model build team uploaded `rev-20260314-b` but forgot to update the tokenizer metadata file (tokenizer.txt). The registry accepted it because we don't have a validation that cross-checks tokenizer compatibility.

alex: assign action owners: cheng -> immediate fix to catalog automation to reject mismatched tokenizer metadata; maria (not in thread) -> follow-up with model build team; product -> ship notice with safe upgrade notes.

sam: I'm going to escalate to oncall lead for a short handoff. @ida can you take and continue for the 09:30 UTC rotation? I'll summarize the state.

ida: I got it. Handoff ack. Saved commands and incident notes in /incidents/INC-20260314-0821/notebook.md

sam: handoff notes: pinned to rev-20260314-a, canary healthy at 5% -> increased to 100%, errors back to baseline. Mitigation: rollback pin applied. Root cause: missing tokenizer metadata for rev-20260314-b. Action items: (1) catalog validation for tokenizer-runs, (2) restore CI to include tokenizer hash check, (3) backfill health-check to detect tokenization regressions in canary.

ida: will continue monitoring and coordinate with cheng for the automation patch. Also will send an interim status update on the incident channel and to SUP-783.

alex: can we confirm no data corruption or persisted bad outputs to customers?

sam: checked logs: malformed tokens were only present in transient responses; for customers that saved outputs, instruct support to flag and re-run generation; no persisted DB writes from system side were affected. Marking potential customer impact as low-medium but visible.

leda: support notes: proactively contacted two users who reported problems; offered to re-run jobs and provided a timeline. Will escalate if enterprise customers surface.

cheng: pushed a hotfix branch to catalog repo: `fix/tokenizer-validate-20260314`. Patch adds pre-promotion validator that compares model artifact tokenizer hash against declared tokenizer. Will open PR and fast-track approval.

cheng: PR link: https://git.example/redwood/catalog/pull/892

sam: thanks. I'm going to de-escalate the pager once we have 30m stability. Leaving this thread for the handoff to @ida.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-20260314-0821 marked: acknowledged -> resolved by sam (mitigation applied). Resolution note: pinned catalog to previous revision; automation patch in progress.

pagerduty: Incident resolved at 08:45 UTC.

ida: taking over post-mortem tasks. I'll schedule a 1h follow-up with model-build + catalog teams, include regression test additions.

alex: nice work all. Please file postmortem and include timeline + customer outreach summary.

sam: closing out. :thumbsup:
